harbor_p06_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_001.text: The eighth week opened with a release for lot R4. The commercial clerk had verified the supported right to move its cleared contents, and Sui Yan's handling office had approved the method. Tub T4 remained under the separate ownership hold. The issued order said the contents must be transferred into a clean approved receiving container before departure. Miao brought the order to the merchant's shore yard and asked for a cart. Yue saw the public disposition entry during her inquiry shift and marked no worker-property change.

harbor_p06_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_002.text: The hired porter arrived before the clean receiving container did. His name was Lu Cheng, and he was paid by the completed trip rather than by waiting time. He carried the narrow route slip whose references Yue had previously questioned. At the shed, an ordinary attendant showed him the full release conditions and pointed to the held-container tag. Lu said he would fetch the replacement. The attendant entered his arrival and departure because the handling lane had begun to attract carriers who thought cleared cargo could simply be taken.

harbor_p06_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_003.text: At noon, He Ming came to the office with a new neighbor's question about safe-contact notices. Yue directed it to the proper clerk and went with her for lunch. They argued over whether a dumpling shop was better than the one near Willow Reach. He Ming defended home fiercely while eating a second harbor dumpling. Yue accused her of preserving the argument by destroying the evidence. The woman laughed with her mouth full. For a few minutes, the harbor's unresolved cargo could not compete with ginger and hot broth.

harbor_p06_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_004.text: The first alarm sounded when they returned. Wen Zhi stood at the commercial window insisting tub T4 had left on a cart. The gate attendant's record showed a contents release, but the transfer line named the same tub as its carrying vessel. The clerk closed further collection on that reference and asked the captain to trace the move. The instruction did not cancel unrelated safe releases. Yue stayed at the public table until asked to help compare the issued order with the gate copy. He Ming went to find the eyewitness.

harbor_p06_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_005.text: The gate copy lacked the sentence requiring transfer into a clean container. It retained the R4 release number and a shorthand description, contents in T4. The full original in the commercial file had not changed. The clerk secured both and recorded the difference. Sui Yan asked where the tub had gone and who authorized the gate attendant to treat its tag as cleared. The attendant said Lu presented a merchant-yard carrying note alongside the truncated copy. He had read them as a route instruction under the valid release.

harbor_p06_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_006.text: Yue copied the differing sentences onto a comparison page under the clerk's supervision. Her inquiry contract permitted relevant discrepancies, not questioning carriers under threat. The copied page identified each source and custodian. The merchant-yard note said take the cleared lot as packed to the east store. It did not mention the held-container condition. Miao had signed it that morning. His signature established the instruction he issued. The question was whether he meant a permitted contents move or chose wording that would bypass a condition he had already received.

harbor_p06_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_007.text: Sui Yan sent ordinary harbor staff to the east store with the limited request to locate and hold the disputed container pending the commercial direction. The note carried no power to seize unrelated goods. Miao was away meeting his employer's arriving representative. A storeman said the R4 lot had already been loaded onto a licensed creek barge for an inner-harbor transfer. He supplied its destination and departure entry. The commercial clerk asked the harbor master to contact the pilot before the barge passed into the outer channel.

harbor_p06_008.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p06_008.text: We need the recorded tub kept available for review. We do not need a chase invented by angry owners. The pilot can receive a harbor master's hold instruction at the inner landing. The passengers and crew remain people with their own safe route. Wen, stay at the public collection point where the status can reach you. Yue, compare the two documents and report only what they say. I will not have anyone leap aboard a moving boat to prove that a container matters.

harbor_p06_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_009.text: Wen Zhi wanted to hire a fast skiff himself. Yan Su arrived from the rigging lane and asked which pilot he intended to use and what boarding authority he possessed. Wen had neither. He slammed his maker's drawing onto the table. Yue saw how close his fear sat to anger. Six tubs were a large portion of his working stock, and two were already difficult to recover clean. She asked whether he wanted the clerk to record the immediate business cost of the unauthorized move. He nodded, breathing hard.

harbor_p06_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_010.text: The harbor master's messenger reached the inner landing before the barge passed. Its pilot, Gao Lin, acknowledged the hold instruction and agreed to berth at the licensed inspection stage. A tide change made the approach difficult. He would use the upstream staging post until the safer interval rather than turn across the current at once. The messenger sent that status back by ordinary runner. Sui Yan recorded the delay. The tub had been located; it had not vanished into a sea large enough to justify every reckless idea.

harbor_p06_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_011.text: Miao returned to find the carrying note on the clerk's table. He admitted signing it. He said the receiving container had failed to arrive, and he expected the yard to hold the lot until the condition could be met. The clerk asked why the note said take as packed rather than wait for transfer. He said it was habitual dispatch wording. Han Pei wrote the explanation as his account. She did not replace the note with a kinder sentence. His habit, if true, had traveled with consequences it could not now erase.

harbor_p06_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_012.text: Lu Cheng came next, brought by a harbor staff request he agreed to answer. He admitted knowing T4 was held because the clerk had explained it before the release. He said the merchant-yard note seemed to authorize a later exception. The attendant had let him through. The commercial clerk showed the full release and asked where an exception had been issued. Lu had no such source. He looked at Miao, who looked back without answering. Their different responsibilities met in a silence neither could use as evidence against the other.

harbor_p06_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_013.text: The gate attendant supplied his own account. He had been covering two collection posts after a colleague left for ordinary care, and the carrying note had seemed to match the valid release number. The supervisor produced the staffing record. It explained pressure without granting permission to skip the held-container condition. Sui Yan requested that future route copies preserve the full conditions or link visibly to the original. The commercial clerk required a correction now. Whether a lasting procedure needed additional staff time would go to the term review rather than become unpaid work by announcement.

harbor_p06_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_014.text: Yue finished the comparison before her shift ended and returned the documents to their keepers. She had not followed the barge. She knew its status through signed messages. Outside, He Ming had found two people who saw T4 on the cart. Their descriptions and times went to the authorized clerk. The woman wanted a swift answer about Miao's intent. Yue said the signed note mattered, as did the carrier's acknowledged knowledge. They still needed to hear the accounts and distinguish what each could reasonably rely on. He Ming groaned but did not leave.

harbor_p06_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_015.text: The inspection stage lay upstream beneath a weathered roof. Yan Su joined its ordinary crew because T4's return would need safe handling, not because he could decide title. Sui Yan sent a licensed handling officer and the relevant technical conditions. Yue would travel there during her next approved outreach shift on the ordinary shore road; no extra ferry expense was required. The distance took nearly an hour on foot. He Ming chose to come privately to support Wen, paying her own meal cost and acquiring no authority over the barge.

harbor_p06_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_016.text: The river changed character beyond the crowded quay. Houses gave way to low gardens, and the smell of cabbage smoke replaced tar. He Ming walked quickly until Yue asked whether she wanted to arrive too tired to listen. The woman slowed reluctantly. She said she hated how much of a rightful claim depended on having time to follow an object. Wen could have worked instead of waiting by the office. Yue agreed. That practical loss could be recorded even while the question of intent remained unresolved. He Ming found the distinction tolerable on an empty path.

harbor_p06_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_017.text: At the upstream stage, Gao Lin stood with his pilot's license tucked inside his coat and a face set against further demands. He had received cargo described by a valid release reference and had not been told the container remained held. The harbor master's instruction gave him a clear reason to stop. He wanted the extra berth fee and crew delay recorded for the proper account. Sui Yan's handling officer checked the condition of T4 from the permitted deck position, then confirmed no new residue leak had been seen.

harbor_p06_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_018.text: The barge also carried three ordinary passengers and a crate of roof tiles unrelated to R4. They had waited long enough to become a committee. One accused Wen Zhi, who had arrived by the public shore cart, of delaying everyone for a dirty barrel. Wen said it was a tub and worth more than the passenger's entire basket. The pilot stepped between them. Yue asked the landing clerk whether the passengers had an ordinary onward option. A licensed shore boat could take them through a safe route when its scheduled crew arrived.

harbor_p06_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_019.text: The shore boat arrived with a mother carrying a sleeping child and an argument about whose place belonged first in the queue. The stage clerk assigned the existing booked order and gave delayed passengers a revised departure time. Nobody received a promise that a cultivator would carry them across. Yue stood aside and watched ordinary transport do its work. He Ming helped a passenger tie a bundle only after being asked. The small act changed the quarrel's tone more effectively than her earlier speech about the value of Wen's tub would have.

harbor_p06_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_020.text: Yan Su inspected the stage's rated tackle before any cargo move. Its ordinary maintenance keeper approved the current arrangement but warned that the rising tide would shorten the set-down margin. The foreman chose to keep T4 aboard until the next safe interval if the transfer could not finish within the mark. Wen objected that waiting would add storage cost. Yan pointed to the barge's secured cargo and said the object was not being lost while it waited. An expensive inconvenience did not become a human emergency because its owner had already suffered another one.

harbor_p06_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_021.text: The first handling interval ended before the receiving platform was ready. Yan stopped the preparation and kept the tub secured aboard. A small gust drove spray across the stage, startling a passenger waiting beyond the rope line. He Ming held her own cup and saw how easily impatience could make the wet boards look like a shortcut. Wen sat down at last. The handling officer gave him a written condition check and expected next interval. The paper did not satisfy him. It helped him stop imagining that silence meant somebody had forgotten his property.

harbor_p06_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_022.text: Yue used the waiting time to speak with the pilot about the route note he had received. He consented to a witnessed copy for the relevant inquiry. It named R4 but described the carrying tub as cleared with contents, a phrase absent from the original order. The merchant storeman had written it. Gao said he would not knowingly carry held cargo without a lawful direction. His statement and copy went to the commercial clerk through the stage's recorded delivery route. Yue retained only her permitted working reference after the source was checked.

harbor_p06_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_023.text: He Ming bought soup from the landing stall and brought Wen a bowl. He offered to reimburse her. She accepted the exact price because she had not meant to give a gift she could ill afford. The exchange surprised Yue by its calm. Earlier, He Ming might have performed generosity as though anyone else's worry outranked her own purse. Now she could be kind and direct about money. Wen ate, still angry, while the woman told him the soup seller's child had renamed every customer according to the hat they wore.

harbor_p06_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_024.text: The child called Yue Four Sleeves, though she had used no qi arms at the stage. Yue asked how he knew. He said a passenger had told him, then asked whether the sleeves could stir soup faster. She told him ordinary stirring already worked. He looked disappointed until He Ming said four spoons would make four different arguments about salt. The boy delighted in that possibility and ran to tell his mother. Yue and He Ming laughed while Wen tried unsuccessfully to hide that he was listening.

harbor_p06_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_025.text: At the next safe interval, the ordinary crew fitted T4's approved sling and lifted it onto the rated receiving platform. Yan Su directed the load movement while the keeper watched the tackle. Yue remained at the dry document point. No ward was needed under the conditions, and no one supplied a dramatic reason to use one. The tub settled onto its cradle. The handling officer checked its tag and condition. Gao signed that the disputed container had left his barge under the recorded hold and transfer direction, not under Wen's personal command.

harbor_p06_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_026.text: Returning the tub to the main hold would add unnecessary handling. The commercial clerk's remote direction authorized secure storage at the inspection stage pending the hearing, with its original claim references and custody intact. Technical clearance still applied to the contents under the approved method; title remained disputed. The stage keeper counted the seals with the handling officer before closing the storage face. Wen received a status receipt. He had helped trace his container, but he did not walk away owning it by virtue of being the loudest person at the stage.

harbor_p06_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_027.text: The pilot's unrelated cargo and passengers continued when the harbor master cleared departure. Gao supplied his additional cost claim through the ordinary port process. The staff would decide responsibility based on the move and instructions, rather than charge the wage guarantee bond. Yue walked back with He Ming under a sky turning pale gold. Their boots carried mud from the gardens, and the woman's temper had finally tired enough to let the evening exist. She said she was glad they had not taken Wen's imagined skiff into the current.

harbor_p06_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_028.text: At the north office the following day, the commercial clerk laid out the document sequence. Full release R4 required a clean receiving container. Miao's signed carrying note said take as packed. The gate copy omitted the condition. The storeman's barge note then called the carrying tub cleared. Lu had been expressly told T4 remained held. The gate attendant relied on incomplete paperwork. Each step could be examined without turning the entire chain into one person's invisible intention. The sources had become specific enough for a reasoned finding after the relevant responses.

harbor_p06_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_029.text: The office copyist, Bao Min, found the preparation entry for the gate packet. It listed two leaves: the release extract and the conditions continuation. The merchant-yard messenger had signed for both. Only the first reached the gate. Bao showed the original preparation note to the authorized clerk and supplied the paper batch reference. The missing leaf had not disappeared between an unwitnessed memory and a convenient accusation. It had a recorded route worth tracing. Yue copied the reference under supervision and left the book on its own shelf.

harbor_p06_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_030.text: The merchant storeman found the second leaf beneath a stack of cleaning estimates. He said he had separated it because its heading looked technical and sent the route extract alone to Lu. Its text expressly retained the T4 hold. The clerk recorded the recovered source and his explanation. Miao said he had expected staff to read both. The storeman asked where that expectation appeared on the signed carrying note. They faced each other across the counter, suddenly understanding that each had relied on a task the other had never clearly accepted.

harbor_p06_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_031.text: Qian Du wanted the yard's reply amended to say the second leaf had been accidentally dropped during transit. The storeman refused because he had placed it among the estimates himself. He was frightened enough to speak softly, yet the distinction held. Han Pei told him the office would retain his account and any later correction with its reason. Qian withdrew the proposed wording before it became a signed source. Yue saw the storeman's fingers unclench when the clerk gave him a copy of what he had actually said.

harbor_p06_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_032.text: Miao waited outside until Qian left. Then he asked the storeman why he had contradicted the representative in front of officials. The man answered that a dropped leaf would make the messenger responsible, and the messenger had brought both. Miao looked down at his own signed note. He had spent days defending habit as an explanation. The storeman had now refused a convenient habit of making blame travel toward someone lower in the yard. Their conversation ended without reconciliation, but Miao stopped asking him to revise the sentence.

harbor_p06_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_033.text: Wen Zhi's canceled customer agreement reached the clerk as a copy with two messages attached. The earlier message objected to a price increase; the later one cited delay in returning the tub. Both might have influenced the cancellation. The reviewer asked Wen to distinguish the amount he expected from a confirmed booking and any income actually lost. He frowned at the pages, then supplied the full exchange. He wanted the improper move recognized without building his claim on a simpler story than the customer had written.

harbor_p06_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_034.text: He Ming sat beside Wen while the clerk explained the cost questions. She had expected him to fight the distinction harder. Outside, he said he had raised his price because cleaning and replacement stock cost more this season. A customer could reasonably refuse it. He hated that the canceled job then became entangled with a container moved against its hold. The account could hurt him even when written honestly. He Ming bought her own bowl of soup and said she was learning that fairness did not guarantee a pleasant ending.

harbor_p06_035.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p06_035.text: I want you to remember how much walking it took to bring the same tub back to a place where a clerk could decide it. The old receipt was not the only thing wrong. Someone had to lose work, hire a cart, wait for a tide, and pay for soup while people explained why no single sentence proved everything. I accept that you must hear the accounts. I am asking you to put the actual costs beside them, so careful words do not become another way the cost disappears.

harbor_p06_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_036.text: The clerk accepted Wen's documented expenses and the pilot's delay claim for the proper process. She asked He Ming which expenses were hers and whether she sought reimbursement under any authorized arrangement. The woman said her walk was voluntary, her soup had been repaid, and she did not claim an invented wage. She wanted the burden described, not falsely priced. Yue liked the precision and saw Han Pei write the distinction in the public incident account. It made He Ming's anger more useful without requiring it to become polite.

harbor_p06_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_037.text: Miao's employer sent a representative named Qian Du to the hearing preparation. Qian wore a coat too clean for the shore yard and kept asking whether the container was worth this much time. Wen supplied the loan agreement and business record. The representative said the merchant had purchased the contents in good faith and should not bear every carrier's mistake. The clerk agreed that separate liability questions needed evidence. She also pointed to the merchant-yard instructions signed by its agent and storeman. Good faith was a claim to examine, not a phrase that closed a file.

harbor_p06_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_038.text: Qian privately told Miao the lost bonus was evidence he had handled the voyage poorly. Miao repeated the sentence to Yue at the public counter, asking how a proper wage payment had become his incompetence. Yue said the harbor had decided the covered claims, not his employer's appraisal. He wanted her to say his term was unfair. She said he could seek advice through the ordinary employment route and provide his documents. He disliked the small answer until Han Pei gave him the actual desk reference, which was more useful than her agreement would have been.

harbor_p06_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_039.text: The cargo hearing was moved by two working days to allow the new document chain and expense claims to receive responses. Unrelated safe releases continued. Wen accepted the delay after getting the new date in writing, though he complained at length. Qin's wage guarantee review did not restart because a tub moved improperly. Its two-hundred-fourteen remainder remained under the original notice conditions. Yue had to explain that to a visitor who heard cargo hearing and imagined every paid wage at risk again. She used the public references, keeping families' private pages closed.

harbor_p06_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_040.text: At home, Han Pei found herself rewriting the same transfer sentence in three different ways. She brought the pages to Yue and asked which was clearest. Yue said all were readable and the route still needed a person to keep the conditions attached. Han looked annoyed, then laughed at her own disappointment. She had wanted language to fix labor. The painted gull sat beside her elbow. Its shape had improved because she used a brush differently, not because she labeled it more carefully. The comparison was so obvious she disliked it.

harbor_p06_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_041.text: They went to the boat painter again on their next free morning. Duan gave Han a small repair edge to practice under supervision, without treating her as a hired painter or giving her the boat's finished surface. Yue sanded a scrap and watched the grain emerge. The repetitive ordinary motion settled thoughts the office had left tangled. Han said she might take a paid beginner session after the inquiry term ended if the schedule allowed. Duan told her to ask about the actual session before inventing a whole new career around one pleasant morning.

harbor_p06_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_042.text: On the way back, Yue admitted she sometimes pictured staying in a town as proof she cared about its people. Han said she sometimes pictured leaving the desk as proof she had become brave. Neither picture contained much work. They laughed at the symmetry. Then the clerk asked whether Yue would leave after twelve weeks. Yue said she did not know. She had an end date and enough money to travel, but the harbor's faces had become harder to fit into a finished commission. Han walked quietly after that answer.

harbor_p06_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_043.text: He Ming's mother began preparing her return to Willow Reach before the month ended. She packed the recovered spoon, then took it out because it belonged to He Jun. He told her to keep it. She said she would make another if he actually used it. The discussion took an entire breakfast. He Ming rolled her eyes but enjoyed hearing a dispute that had nothing to do with sealed cargo or missing names. Her mother chose the ordinary ferry day based on water and her own preference, rather than waiting for her children to agree on everything.

harbor_p06_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_044.text: He Jun arranged to escort her as far as the creek connection before returning to the harbor for his own paid work. His private debt plan remained his responsibility and did not draw from He Ming's wage. He wrote the intended collection points before departure, as he had promised. His sister inspected the page and said a delivered note was better than another noble speech. He bowed with exaggerated solemnity. Their mother told him not to perform while carrying the kettle. He nearly spilled it, which settled the argument in laughter.

harbor_p06_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_045.text: At the tea stall, Fen's father asked whether she wanted to visit Willow Reach with He Ming's mother. Fen said she wanted to complete the binder's trial copying session first. Luo had not yet heard about it. The girl showed him a page of practiced characters and expected criticism of the uneven ones. He admired the clear heading and asked how much the session cost. The binder offered a short paid trial, not a purchase of apprenticeship. Fen would decide after seeing the work. Her father's question stayed practical, which pleased her.

harbor_p06_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_046.text: The trial required sorting damaged page edges, checking repeated labels, and copying a short shop notice without losing a line. Fen made two errors and corrected them before the owner pointed them out. She earned the agreed trial pay. The binder offered regular small shifts if the tea seller's schedule allowed, without demanding she abandon the stall immediately. Fen negotiated the times with both adults. Yue watched the girl carry her new wage home and thought how different this was from being carried as the daughter attached to a missing man's claim.

harbor_p06_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_047.text: Fen's copying trial brought a blot across the shop notice's final line. She wanted to scrape it away and pretend the page had survived. The binder showed her how scraping thinned the paper and offered a clean sheet for a fresh copy within the trial task. Fen redid it, angry with herself. Luo Jian arrived after work and admired the finished page. She showed him the spoiled one too. He said his camp accident began with trying to make a hurried cut look already finished. She asked him not to turn every ink mark into wisdom.

harbor_p06_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_048.text: They laughed, then examined the spoiled page together. Fen had rushed the last line because she wanted to prove she could finish before the experienced copyist. The owner had never required that race. Luo said he used to compete with men who could carry larger bundles and called it earning. Fen said his contest made her carry papers across the harbor. He accepted the rebuke. Her new work would have its own temptations. She preferred seeing them named while her father was there to annoy her.

harbor_p06_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_049.text: Dai Min began mending nets for a shore seller at a rate she negotiated herself. He Ming brought a torn net as ordinary paid work and sat nearby while the woman repaired it. Neither spoke about the comb. Dai asked whether He Jun would accompany their mother home. When He Ming answered, she said she hoped the journey went easily. The conversation moved through small things without becoming avoidance. Grief could share a room with a price, a needle, and a question about someone else's living family.

harbor_p06_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_050.text: The net seller offered Dai more work than she could complete in the promised interval. She refused the extra piece and asked for a later date. He Ming heard the answer and admired it. At the packing lane, she had been accepting additional favors because people knew she helped claimants. That evening, she told a foreman she could carry his private letter only if he used the normal collection route or paid an agreed messenger. Her neighbor's need did not turn every other person's convenience into her appointment.

harbor_p06_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_051.text: Deren's temporary stock-checking task reached its agreed end during the eighth week. His clinician allowed more ordinary walking but continued to restrict wet-step climbing and heavy bracing. The maintenance office offered a new bounded seated task with its own pay and dates because the inspection review needed item lists checked. He accepted after inspecting the duties. Yan Su did not speak for him. The men had learned to argue in terms of actual tasks instead of whether accepting restriction made Deren useless. Bo still supplied terrible jokes about royalty payments.

harbor_p06_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_052.text: The ordinary review clerk asked Deren what the platform failure had cost beyond treatment. He named missed shifts, help with walking, and a broken work shoe. The immediate support account had paid prescribed care; lost-work compensation awaited the reasoned responsibility findings. Deren supplied receipts where he had them and identified estimates where he did not. The review would decide, rather than inventing exact figures because the harm was obvious. Yue heard the public status and did not promise him the unused wage bond as a quick answer. He would have disliked such a promise once it failed.

harbor_p06_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_053.text: Sui Yan attended the platform review as the person responsible for the handling operation, not as its judge. She supplied the work plan, stop instruction, rescue record, and post-failure inspection. Yan supplied the routine he had used and the changes proposed. The carpenter supplied the rot findings. Their willingness to answer did not create their own acquittal. An independent harbor reviewer would compare duty, condition, notice, and actual decisions. Yue found the separation awkward to watch because she liked the captain and foreman. Liking them did not settle Deren's question.

harbor_p06_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_054.text: The captain noticed Yue's discomfort afterward. She asked whether the record looked worse because they admitted so much. Yue said it looked more usable. Sui said usable records could still lead to consequences she feared. Her license supported her livelihood. She had spent years making herself the person others relied on, and could not bear being remembered only for a rotten brace she had not personally inspected. Yue said no one deserved a false story to protect them. Sui nodded, then asked to walk alone for a while.

harbor_p06_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_055.text: Wen's temporary container loss reached another practical consequence when a customer canceled a planned borrowing arrangement. He added the customer's dated message to his expense claim, acknowledging that part of the expected income had never been guaranteed. The commercial reviewer would decide which documented loss followed the improper move and which remained ordinary business risk. Miao resented every new page. Wen said he resented needing them. Their exchange happened in the public window where the clerk could stop it before it became a threat. Yue arrived to find both men abruptly polite.

harbor_p06_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_056.text: The gate attendant's supervisor assigned a second trained person during the busiest release interval for the remainder of the cargo operation. Ordinary staffing funds covered the change after approval; Yue's inquiry did not pay salaries silently. The attendant was required to check held-container tags against full conditions before allowing a carrying move. He accepted the immediate instruction and asked for written guidance on conflicting notes. The office supplied it. Lasting staffing would be considered separately. A current correction could protect the next cart without claiming the whole harbor had been repaired.

harbor_p06_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_057.text: A public transfer notice showed a drawing of a tub beside two separate boxes: contents and container. Han Pei asked the painter Duan to review whether the drawing was legible, as a bounded paid task through the copying line. The agreed charge was four copper for the illustration and reproduction preparation. Combined with the previous two, copying expenses now used six of twenty-four, leaving eighteen. Yue checked the receipt and laughed when Duan complained Han's drawn gull had too much authority over the office window. The clerk moved the board again.

harbor_p06_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_058.text: The notice helped one carrier ask the right question before loading and did nothing for another who never looked at it. Yan Su said a sign could assist a task but could not perform it. He Ming said he had become as tiresome as Han Pei. The clerk, present at the quay, said she considered that a promotion. They laughed while the carrier found his own assigned attendant. Yue liked how their differences had begun to create jokes. The humor did not need everyone to agree about which office failed first.

harbor_p06_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_059.text: On the eighth week's last inquiry shift, Yue assembled the improper-transfer sources for the coming hearing. She had completed sixteen half-days and earned thirty-two copper under the initial forty-eight wage line. Ferry expenses remained six; interpreters six; copying now six. The various documents stayed with their official keepers after comparison. Tub T4 remained secured at the licensed inspection stage, while R4's permitted disposition awaited the commercial direction after the new claims. She recorded no higher cultivation, no acquired container, and no authority to decide intent herself.

harbor_p06_060.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_060.text: The afternoon brought a brief letter from the forest commission acknowledging Yue's arrival and wishing her fair roads. It described a repaired boundary marker and nothing urgent. She read it twice. The forest no longer needed her immediate answer. Its ordinary work had continued, just as the harbor would someday continue. She put the letter among her personal notes and went downstairs to supper. The kite fish swung in the draft above the door, still claiming a sea it could not reach. Yue touched its patched tail and left it hanging.

harbor_p06_061.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_061.text: He Ming watched the ordinary ferry take her mother toward Willow Reach. He Jun stood beside the older woman with the kettle between his feet. Their final wave continued long after faces blurred. He Ming did not cry until Yue said they should move from the unloading lane. Then she laughed at the absurd timing and wiped her face with the scarf. She had finally received the family reunion she wanted. It included another departure, properly announced this time, and a room that would be quieter tonight.

harbor_p06_062.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_062.text: Yue walked her home and accepted tea from the cup her mother had left behind. The woman said she would miss being criticized for folding bedding incorrectly. Yue said that seemed a difficult thing to explain to people outside the family. He Ming answered that most important things were. They opened the window to the evening air. At the quay, a worker called the tide reading to another worker who repeated it clearly. The ordinary sound reached the room without requiring either woman to turn it into a lesson.

harbor_p06_063.speaker: narrator
harbor_p06_063.text: The hearing notice for the ninth week arrived at the commercial board before dusk. It named the container loan, contents rights, safe cleaning obligations, improper transfer, and documented costs as distinct questions. It named the parties and source access they could use, with private employment pages protected where irrelevant. Wen read it in silence. Miao stood beside him this time rather than opposite. Neither called the document fair aloud. Both knew what they needed to answer. The harbor had recovered a tub and acquired a harder account of why it had left.
